problems.title: A rational inequality in 2 to the x
problems.question: Solve $1/(2^x-1)>1/(1-2^{x-1})$.
problems.idea: Substitute t=2ˣ and make a sign chart.
steps: Exclude t=1,2. The critical values are 1,4/3,2.
The expression is positive on (1,4/3) and (2,∞), and negative on the other positive intervals.
Since 2ˣ increases, these intervals give 0<x<log₂(4/3) or x>1.

problems.title: Compare inscribed square and disk areas
problems.question: A cone has volume 17.5π. Find the volume of an inscribed regular square pyramid.
problems.idea: The pyramid and cone have the same height, so their volume ratio equals their base-area ratio.
formulas: Inscribed square area=2R²; disk area=πR²; V=base area·h/3.
steps: The square diagonal is 2R, so its area is (2R)²/2=2R².
The pyramid volume is (2/π) times the cone volume.

problems.title: An obtuse triangle rotated around a leg
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 6 cm and apex angle 120°. It rotates around one equal side. Find the resulting volume.
problems.idea: An obtuse angle produces a large cone with a smaller cone removed.
steps: Place the apex A at axial coordinate 0 and the end of the rotation side B at 6. The other vertex C projects to -3 and is 3√3 from the axis.
The outer cone has height 9 and radius 3√3. The missing inner cone has height 3 and the same radius.
Subtract: V=π(3√3)²(9-3)/3=54π.

problems.title: Sphere inscribed in a cone frustum
problems.question: A cone frustum has base radii 2 cm and 8 cm and contains a sphere tangent to both bases and the lateral surface. Find the sphere volume.
problems.idea: Its axial section is a tangential isosceles trapezoid.
formulas: In a tangential quadrilateral, opposite-side sums are equal; slant²=h²+(R-r)²; sphere V=4πρ³/3.
steps: The axial bases are 4 and 16, so twice the slant is 20 and the slant is 10.
Then h=√(10²-6²)=8. A sphere tangent to both base planes has diameter h, so ρ=4.
Its volume is 4π·4³/3=256π/3.

problems.title: A square identifies the only excluded point
problems.question: Solve $2\log_8(x-2)-\log_8(x-3)>2/3$.
problems.idea: Combine logarithms, keeping the original domain.
steps: The domain is x>3. Since base 8 increases, (x-2)²/(x-3)>4.
Here x-3>0, so multiply to get (x-2)²>4(x-3).
This simplifies to (x-4)²>0, excluding only x=4.

problems.title: The shaded region lies beneath two curves
problems.question: Describe the solution region of $2\lg x-\lg y\ge1$, $y+x^2-1\le0$.
problems.idea: Rewrite the logarithmic condition as a bound on y.
steps: The logarithms require x>0,y>0. The first inequality gives y≤x²/10; the second gives y≤1-x².
The curves meet when x²/10=1-x², giving x=√(10/11).
Include both curved top boundaries; exclude the x-axis and the endpoints x=0,1 because y must be positive.

problems.title: Four roots require two positive logarithmic magnitudes
problems.question: Find all a for which $(\log_3x)^2-|\log_3x|+a=0$ has four distinct real solutions.
problems.idea: Each positive magnitude t=|log₃x| gives two x-values.
formulas: t²-t+a=0; sum of roots=1, product=a, discriminant=1-4a.
steps: Two distinct positive t-roots are necessary and sufficient for four distinct x-values 3^t and 3^(-t).
Distinct roots require a<1/4. Their sum is positive, so both are positive exactly when their product a>0.
At a=0 the t-root 0 gives just x=1, yielding three x-roots. At a=1/4 the repeated t-root gives only two.

problems.title: Split before squaring a radical inequality
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{1-9(\log_{1/8}x)^2}>1-4\log_{1/8}x$.
problems.idea: A negative right-hand side makes the inequality automatic.
steps: For t>1/4, the right side is negative, so every t in (1/4,1/3] works.
For t≤1/4 the right side is nonnegative. Squaring is equivalent to 1-9t²>(1-4t)², or t(25t-8)<0.
This gives 0<t<8/25; intersecting with t≤1/4 leaves 0<t≤1/4. Together the cases give 0<t≤1/3.
Because the base 1/8 decreases, this becomes (1/8)^(1/3)≤x<1.

problems.title: The domain reduces an inequality to two checks
problems.question: Solve $(\sqrt{x^2-4x+3}+1)\log_5(x/5)+\dfrac{\log_5(\sqrt{8x-2x^2-6}+5)}{\sin(\pi x/2)}\le0$.
problems.idea: The two square roots can coexist only at their shared zeros.
steps: The first radicand requires x≤1 or x≥3; the second requires 1≤x≤3. Their intersection is {1,3}.
Both candidates have positive logarithm arguments and nonzero sine denominators.
At x=1 the expression is -1+1=0, so it qualifies.
At x=3 it is log₅(3/5)-1<0, so it also qualifies.
